preamble: Backing of the open front or central vowel [a] to the open back vowel [ɑ]. In southern British English the long [aː] that arose in the 17th century by lengthening before /r/ and before /f, θ, s/ was backed to [ɑː], giving Received Pronunciation cart /kɑːt/, cast /kɑːst/ and path /pɑːθ/. In Old French, /a/ before a preconsonantal /s/ that was debuccalized and lost became a long back /ɑː/ (masle > mâle /mɑːl/, paste > pâte /pɑt/). In Standard Arabic, /a/ and /aː/ are retracted to [ɑ] in the environment of the emphatic consonants; in Cairene pronunciation the retraction spreads to every vowel of the word.

examples.note: Wikipedia gives the stages [kast] > [kaːst] > [kɑːst], with the last step labelled backing of /aː/.
The preconsonantal /s/ became /h/ and was lost, leaving a long vowel; for /a/ the lengthening came with a change in quality to back /ɑː/.
